notes.claim: On discharge, lead at the negative plate reacts with sulphuric acid to form lead sulphate, freeing electrons.
At the positive plate, lead oxide reacts with sulphuric acid, again forming lead sulphate.
On discharge both plates become lead sulphate and the sulphuric acid is used up, leaving water behind.
The acid concentration rises during charging and falls during discharge, so charging runs the discharge reaction backwards.
The nominal voltage of a lead-acid cell is 2 V, but a charged and rested cell measures about 2.1 V open circuit.
A primary cell is single-use and cannot be recharged; a secondary cell, such as lead-acid, can be recharged by an external power source.
